## 5E1

2 and 4 are clearly multiple regressions. 3 I think is a single regression because of the parameterization, but of course it's got two variables as inputs on the right hand side so I could see classifying it either way.

## 5E2

Where $ad$ is animal diversity, $lat$ is latitude, and $pd$ is plant diversity.

$$E(ad_i) = \alpha + \beta_1 lat_i + pd_i$$

## 5E3

For student $i$, we suggest that lab funding $f$ and size $s$ jointly contribute to time to degree, and we expect these relationships to be negative.

$$E(t_i) = \alpha + \beta_1 f_i + \beta_2 s_i$$

## 5E4

1, 2, 4 are definitely equivalent. 5 is really funky. I'm not completely sure what that would do, as for category A, we'd return a -2 there, which the model can estimate a value for. So I think it'd actually shake out the same as the others, but it's a weird way to do it!

## 5H1

Here's our DAG

```{r}
d1 <- dagify(d~a,
             a~m)
ggdag(d1) + theme_dag()
```

It suggests that $m\perp d | a$, which we can check with dagitty

```{r}
dagitty::impliedConditionalIndependencies(d1)
```

We can empirically check this with a visual and a regression.

```{r}
data("WaffleDivorce")
ggplot(WaffleDivorce,
       aes(x = Marriage, y = Divorce)) + 
  geom_point()
```

Looks like an unconditional linear association, which is what we'd expect with the DAG.

```{r, results = "hide"}
m1 <- brm(Divorce~ Marriage + MedianAgeMarriage,
          data = WaffleDivorce)
```

Looks like a pretty clear indpendence.

```{r}
m1_post <- as_draws_df(m1)
ggplot(m1_post,
       aes(x = b_Marriage)) + 
  stat_slabinterval()
```

Yeah, lots of posterior mass centered at zero. We could push this further and evaluate the density of the parameter under an unconditional model, but the visual already tells us there's an association there at a bivariate level. This evidence is consistent with the pipe DAG m->a->d

## 5H2

Here, we'll estimate a multivariate model for $a$ and $m$ to simulate the dependencies

```{r, results = "hide"}
# use bf to specify a model with two response variables
# vignette here: https://paulbuerkner.com/brms/articles/brms_multivariate.html

m2_d <- bf(Divorce ~ Marriage + MedianAgeMarriage)
m2_a <- bf(MedianAgeMarriage ~ Marriage)
m2 <- brm(m2_a+m2_d, data = WaffleDivorce)
summary(m2)
```
